role: The server half of one player's block interaction: the game type, the dig progress machine (click, per-tick damage, finish and cancel packets) and the harvest and right-click-use paths.
scope_reason: Every survival dig and every right-click runs through it; world.conf switches none of it (adventure mode is simply never used and creative only in dev snapshots).

notes: The dig machine (dig.c) ports the whole click/tick/finish/cancel cycle including the destroyBlockInWorldPartially stage history; survival.c's surv_server_dig_packet and surv_server_dig_update (survival.h:555-559) are the server_player-side drivers. test_dig.c checks the dig ops against the oracle's dig probe recordings under out/java/dig. The creative and adventure modes are not part of any recorded scenario. Not gaps (triage 2026-09-25, out/plan/remaining-2026-09-25.md): creative, adventure, hardcore or game-type path; the game is survival at the pinned difficulty. Formerly listed as missing: The game-type state (setGameType, getGameType, initializeGameType) is not ported: the native engine plays survival only and dig.h:34 documents adventure as out of scope. The creative-only branches' packet side (tryHarvestBlock's S23PacketBlockChange, the sword guard) is not a ported machine; dev ops drive creative actions through csrc/engine/dev.c instead. ItemInWorldManager.setWorld's rebinding is folded into serverreplay.c's transfer bookkeeping rather than existing as its own symbol.
